topics.title: The 把 construction
topics.description: Putting the object first to talk about what you do TO it

guide.intro: 把 (bǎ) is one of the most distinctive features of Mandarin grammar. It moves the object before the verb to say "take X and do something to it". You'll hear it constantly — and English doesn't have a clean equivalent.

sections.text: The basic shape

Normal Chinese order is Subject–Verb–Object. With 把, you reorder to Subject–把–Object–Verb–(extra). The "extra" part is crucial — 把 sentences almost never end on a bare verb. There has to be a result, location, or change attached.

rows: 我 把 门 关 上
他 把 苹果 吃 了
请 放 书 在 桌子 上
请 把 书 放 在 桌子 上

sections.text: When to use 把
Use 把 when you want to emphasize what HAPPENS TO a specific, known object — moving it, finishing it, changing it, putting it somewhere. Both speaker and listener know which object you mean.

rows.source: 我 把 作业 做 完 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le.

rows.source: 请 把 窗户 打 开。
他 把 杯子 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Tā bǎ bēizi dǎ pò le.

sections.text: If you can't say what HAPPENS TO the object, don't use 把. "我 把 苹果 喜欢" is wrong — 喜欢 (like) doesn't change the apple.
What can't follow 把
把 needs a verb that physically affects the object. Verbs that don't qualify: feeling/perception verbs (爱, 喜欢, 觉得, 知道), existence verbs (有, 是), and most stative or motion-only verbs (来, 去, 走).

rows.source: 我 喜欢 这 本 书。
rows.translation: I like this book. (NOT 我 把 这 本 书 喜欢)

rows.source: 他 知道 答案。
rows.translation: He knows the answer. (NOT 他 把 答案 知道)

sections.text: Negation: 没 / 不 goes BEFORE 把

rows.source: 我 没 把 作业 做 完。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ méi bǎ zuòyè zuò wán.

rows.source: 请 不要 把 门 关 上。
rows.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào bǎ mén guān shàng.

topics.title: The 被 passive
topics.description: When something happens TO the subject — usually unpleasantly

guide.intro: 被 (bèi) is the passive marker — "got / was done by". It's the mirror image of 把: where 把 puts the actor first and the patient mid-sentence, 被 puts the patient (victim) first.

sections.text: The basic shape
Pattern: Patient + 被 + (Agent) + Verb + result. The agent is optional — drop it if it's unknown or obvious.

rows.source: 我 的 手机 被 偷 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.

rows.source: 杯子 被 他 打 破 了。
rows.pinyin: Bēizi bèi tā dǎ pò le.
rows.translation: The cup was broken by him.

rows.source: 钱 被 老板 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Qián bèi lǎobǎn ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: The money was taken by the boss.

sections.text: 把 vs 被 — same event, different POV

rows: 他 把 杯子 打 破 了
杯子 被 他 打 破 了
小偷 偷 了 我 的 手机
我 的 手机 被 (小偷) 偷 了

sections.text: Mandarin's 被 has a slightly negative or unfortunate flavor — it's used much more often for bad things (got stolen, broken, scolded) than for neutral or good ones. Sentences like "I was praised" (我 被 表扬 了) work but feel marked.
叫 / 让 — informal alternatives
In speech, 叫 (jiào) or 让 (ràng) often replace 被. They sound more casual — but unlike 被, they REQUIRE an agent.

rows.source: 我 的 钱 让 他 拿走 了。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de qián ràng tā ná zǒu le.
rows.translation: My money got taken by him.

rows.source: 他 叫 老师 批评 了。
rows.translation: He got scolded by the teacher.

sections.text: Negation
Same as 把 — put 没 BEFORE 被.

rows.source: 我 的 手机 没 被 偷。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi bèi tōu.

sections.text: Two flavors of 了
Mandarin uses 了 in two distinct slots, and 把 / 被 sentences often need both. Knowing which is which is the difference between a complete sentence and a fragment.

rows: Something is now different / new situation

rows.source: 他 吃 了 三 个 苹果。
rows.pinyin: Tā chī le sān ge píngguǒ.
rows.translation: He ate three apples. (perfective 了₁ — action complete)

rows.source: 下 雨 了。
rows.translation: It's raining now. (sentence 了₂ — change of state, didn't use to be)

rows.source: 已经 下 了 三 天 雨 了。
rows.pinyin: Yǐjīng xià le sān tiān yǔ le.
rows.translation: It's been raining for three days. (BOTH 了 — completed duration AND ongoing relevance)

sections.text: Quick test: if the 了 hugs the verb (verb 了 object), it's 了₁. If the 了 is at the very end of the sentence, it's 了₂. Same character, different jobs.

topics.title: Giving with 给
topics.description: 给 as both "give" and a coverb meaning "for / to"

guide.intro: 给 (gěi) wears two hats. As a main verb it means "give". As a coverb sitting before another verb, it marks the recipient or beneficiary — "for someone", "to someone". Both uses are everywhere.

sections.text: 给 as main verb — "give"
Pattern: Subject + 给 + recipient + thing. Two objects in a row, recipient first.

rows.source: 我 给 他 一 本 书。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā yì běn shū.

rows.source: 妈妈 给 我 钱。

sections.text: 给 as coverb — "for / to"
Sandwiched before another verb, 给 marks who benefits or receives the action. Pattern: Subject + 给 + recipient + verb + object.

rows.source: 我 给 你 买 了 一 杯 咖啡。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ mǎi le yì bēi kāfēi.
rows.translation: I bought you a coffee. (the buying is FOR you)

rows.source: 他 给 妈妈 打 电话。
rows.translation: He's calling mom. (the call is TO mom)

rows.source: 请 给 我 介绍 一下。

sections.text: Notice how 给 you 买 (buy for you) and 给 妈妈 打 电话 (call mom) both keep 给 + person BEFORE the main verb. English flips this around — Chinese is rigid about the order.

topics.title: How well? — 得 complement
topics.description: Modify a verb with how it was done — 得 + adjective

guide.intro: 得 (de) lets you describe the manner or degree of an action: not WHAT you did, but HOW WELL or HOW MUCH. It's the closest Mandarin gets to English adverbs.

sections.text: The basic pattern
Pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + (very) + Adjective. Note the position of 很 — almost always required to keep the sentence sounding natural.

rows.source: 他 跑 得 很 快。
她 唱 得 很 好。
我 睡 得 不 好。

sections.text: When the verb has an object
If your verb takes an object, you have to repeat the verb. Mandarin can't have an object AND a 得 phrase on the same verb. Pattern: Subject + Verb + Object, Verb + 得 + adjective.

rows.source: 他 说 中文 说 得 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: He speaks Chinese very well. (literally: "speaks Chinese, speaks very well")

rows.source: 她 写 字 写 得 很 漂亮。
rows.pinyin: Tā xiě zì xiě de hěn piàoliang.

sections.text: Common mistake: "他 说 中文 得 很 好" — wrong. The verb has to repeat. Or you can drop the object: "他 中文 说 得 很 好" also works.
Three different 得 / 的 / 地

rows: after a verb: how it was done
走 得 慢 — walks slowly

sections.text: All three are pronounced "de" (neutral tone) — only writing distinguishes them. Pay attention to position: 的 between nouns, 地 before verbs, 得 after verbs.
Negation: not 不 before 得 — 不 before the adjective

rows.source: 他 跑 得 不 快。
我 唱 得 不 好。

topics.title: Verb complements
topics.description: Resultative & directional complements — what English handles with separate words, Mandarin stitches onto the verb.

guide.intro: English says "I looked but didn't see it" with two verbs. Mandarin says 我 看 了 但 没 看见 — the result (见 = perceive) is glued to the verb (看 = look). This is the resultative complement, and it's everywhere. Directional complements work the same way but for motion.

sections.text: Resultative complements
Verb + result. The verb is the action you tried; the second character tells the outcome. Without the complement, you're only saying you DID the action, not that it WORKED.
Directional complements
Verb + direction. 上 (up), 下 (down), 进 (in), 出 (out), 回 (back), 过 (across). Compound forms add 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker): 上来, 下去, 进来, 出去 …

rows.source: 他 走 上 楼。
他 走 上 来 了。
她 跑 出 教室。
rows.translation: She runs out of the classroom.

sections.text: Potential complement: 得 / 不

To say you CAN or CAN'T achieve the result, insert 得 (able) or 不 (not able) between the verb and the complement: 看得见 / 看不见, 听得懂 / 听不懂. This is NOT the same as 可以 + verb — that asks for permission. Potential complements ask whether the result is achievable.
English speakers reach for 可以 看见 ("can see"). That's wrong. Use 看得见 ("see-able") for "I can see it".

exercises.prompt: Build "He walked up onto the stage"
exercises.answer: 他 走 上 舞台
exercises.explanation: 走上 = walk + onto / up. The direction follows the verb directly.

exercises.prompt: "她 跑 出 教室" means:
options: She runs out of the classroom
She walks out of the classroom
exercises.answer: She runs out of the classroom
exercises.explanation: 跑 = run; 出 = out. Verb + direction = motion + path.

exercises.prompt: Build "Please take the book down (off the shelf)"
exercises.answer: 请 把 书 拿 下 来
exercises.explanation: 拿下来 = take + down + toward speaker. Classic 把-construction with directional.

exercises.prompt: Which means "He walks into the room"?
options: 他 走 上 房间
他 走 进 房间
他 走 出 房间
他 走 下 房间
exercises.answer: 他 走 进 房间
exercises.explanation: 进 = into / enter. Pair it with motion verbs (走, 跑, 跳) for entering.

exercises.prompt: Build "The cat jumped down from the table"
exercises.answer: 猫 从 桌子 上 跳 下 来
exercises.explanation: 跳下来 = jump + down + toward speaker. 从…上 frames the starting point.

exercises.prompt: "他 拿 上 一 杯 茶" means:
options: He takes a cup of tea up / picks up a cup of tea
He drinks a cup of tea
He takes a cup of tea down
He breaks a cup of tea
exercises.answer: He takes a cup of tea up / picks up a cup of tea
exercises.explanation: 拿上 = take + up. Picture lifting it from a surface.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "他 跑 ___ 房间 找 钥匙" (He ran INTO the room to look for keys)
exercises.explanation: 进 = into. 跑进 = run into a space.

exercises.prompt: Which direction fits "take down (from up high)"?
exercises.explanation: 下 = down / off. 拿下 = take down.

exercises.prompt: Build "She ran out of the supermarket"
exercises.answer: 她 跑 出 超市
exercises.explanation: 跑出 = run out (of). The location comes right after.

exercises.prompt: Which is grammatical for "He climbed up the mountain"?
options: 他 上 爬 山
他 爬 上 山
他 山 爬 上
他 上 山 爬
exercises.answer: 他 爬 上 山
exercises.explanation: Verb first, direction second, object last: 爬 (climb) + 上 (up) + 山 (mountain).

exercises.prompt: Which directional means "into"?
Build "He walked into the office"
exercises.answer: 他 走 进 办公室

lessons.title: Compound directionals: 上来 / 下去 / 进来 / 出去
lessons.description: Add 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker)

exercises.prompt: You're upstairs. Your friend is downstairs. You shout "快 上来!" — what are you telling them?
exercises.explanation: 上来 = up + toward speaker. You're up; they're below; you want them to ascend to YOU.

exercises.prompt: You're upstairs and your friend wants to come up. They look up and say "我 上 ___ 了". Pick the right complement.
exercises.explanation: Speaker is moving TOWARD you (the listener, who is up). From their perspective, you are the destination — 来 (come). 上来 = coming up.

exercises.prompt: Contrast: "她 跑 出 去 了" vs "她 跑 出 来 了"
options: First: ran out (away from speaker). Second: ran out (toward speaker).
First: ran in. Second: ran out.
exercises.answer: First: ran out (away from speaker). Second: ran out (toward speaker).
exercises.explanation: 去 = away from speaker. 来 = toward speaker. The direction relative to YOU is the key insight English doesn't bake into motion verbs.

exercises.prompt: You're inside. Tell someone outside "Come in!"
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. Standard invitation to come inside.

exercises.prompt: You're inside. You tell a noisy person "出去!". What did you say?
exercises.explanation: 出去 = out + away from speaker. Sharp dismissal.

exercises.prompt: Build "He walked down (away from me)"
exercises.answer: 他 走 下 去 了
exercises.explanation: 下去 = down + away from speaker. 了 marks the completed motion.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.spokenText: 你 快 上 来 吧
options: 你 快 上 来 吧
你 快 下 去 吧
你 快 进 来 吧
你 快 出 去 吧
exercises.answer: 你 快 上 来 吧
exercises.explanation: 上来 (shàng lái) — come up. Common invitation when speaker is above the listener.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 出去 (chū qù) — please go out / leave. Contrast with 进来 (come in).

exercises.prompt: You're at the bottom of the stairs. You call to a friend at the top: "快 ___!" (Come down quickly!)
exercises.explanation: Speaker is below. Friend should DESCEND TOWARD speaker → 下来.

exercises.prompt: Your friend (inside) calls you (outside): "快 进 来 吧!" — what are they saying?
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. They're inside; you should enter TOWARD them.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right "come down to me":

Fill: "快 ___ 来 吃饭" (downstairs, kids upstairs)

Tap what you hear
Build "He walked out" (away from us)
exercises.answer: 他 走 出 去 了

exercises.prompt: Why does direction matter with 来/去?
options: 来 = toward speaker; 去 = away from speaker
exercises.answer: 来 = toward speaker; 去 = away from speaker

exercises.prompt: Fill: "她 跑 出 ___ 了" (toward us)
Pick the right phrase: "He brought it up here" (you're upstairs)
options: 他 拿 上 来 了

exercises.answer: 他 拿 上 来 了

lessons.title: Potential: 看得见 vs 看不见
lessons.description: 得 / 不 inserted INSIDE the complement — not the same as 可以

exercises.prompt: "我 看得见 那 个 招牌" means:
options: I'm not allowed to see the sign
I can see the sign (it's visible to me)
I want to see the sign
I have to see the sign
exercises.answer: I can see the sign (it's visible to me)
exercises.explanation: 看得见 = see-able. 得 sits between 看 and 见 to say the result IS achievable.

exercises.prompt: "我 听不懂 他 说 的 话" means:
options: I refuse to listen to him
I'm not allowed to listen to him
I can't understand what he says (it's not comprehensible to me)
I don't want to listen to him
exercises.answer: I can't understand what he says (it's not comprehensible to me)
exercises.explanation: 听不懂 = un-understandable-by-listening. 不 inserted between 听 and 懂. The result isn't achievable.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: which is WRONG for "I can see"?
options: Both 'B' and 'C' — use potential complement 看得见 for visibility
exercises.answer: Both 'B' and 'C' — use potential complement 看得见 for visibility
exercises.explanation: 可以 / 能 ask about PERMISSION or general capability. 看得见 specifically says "the sight reaches me / is visible." Native speakers say 看得见, not 可以 看见.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "老师 的 字 太 小, 我 看 ___ 见" (I can't see — the writing is too small)
exercises.explanation: Negative potential: 看不见 = can't see. 不 goes between verb and complement.

exercises.prompt: Build "I can understand what you say"
exercises.answer: 我 听得懂 你 说 的 话
exercises.explanation: 听得懂 — single chunk: verb + 得 + result. Don't break it into 可以 + 听懂.

exercises.prompt: "这 道 题 我 做 不 出 来" means:
options: I refuse to do this problem
I haven't done this problem yet
I can't figure out this problem (can't produce a solution)
exercises.answer: I can't figure out this problem (can't produce a solution)
exercises.explanation: 做不出来 = unable to produce / work out. 不 sits inside the verb-complement compound.

exercises.source: 我 看不见 黑板
acceptableAnswers: The blackboard isn't visible to me
exercises.explanation: 看不见 — classic complaint from the back of the classroom.

exercises.prompt: Pick the natural Mandarin for "I can hear it" (the sound reaches me):
exercises.explanation: 听得见 = hear-able. Use for perception capability, not permission.

exercises.prompt: Form the question "Can you understand?" (comprehension):
options: 你 能 听 吗?
你 可以 听 吗?
你 想 听 吗?
exercises.explanation: 听得懂 吗 — standard "do you follow?" Distinct from asking permission.

exercises.prompt: Build "I can't finish this book" (don't have the ability to finish it)
exercises.answer: 我 看 不 完 这 本 书
exercises.explanation: 看不完 = can't finish reading. Different from 没 看完 (haven't finished). 不 = capability; 没 = past fact.

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between 看见 and 看得见?
options: 看见 = past fact 'saw'; 看得见 = current capability 'can see'
exercises.answer: 看见 = past fact 'saw'; 看得见 = current capability 'can see'

exercises.prompt: Build "I can hear it clearly"
exercises.answer: 我 听得 很 清楚

exercises.prompt: Fill: "这 个 字 我 看 ___ 见" (potential: cannot see)

lessons.description: Resultative + directional + potential — pick the right form

exercises.prompt: Translate: "He climbed up the mountain (and made it to the top)"
options: 他 爬 上 山 了
他 想 爬 山
他 不 爬 山
exercises.answer: 他 爬 上 山 了
exercises.explanation: 爬上 = climb + up (result reached). 了 confirms completion.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: which is WRONG for "I can't understand the news"?
options: 我 听 不 懂 新闻
我 可以 不 听懂 新闻
听 不 懂 新闻
exercises.answer: 我 可以 不 听懂 新闻
exercises.explanation: 可以 不 听懂 is unnatural. Use the potential complement 听不懂 — don't try to bolt 可以 onto a resultative.

exercises.prompt: Build "Please come in" (you're inside; addressee is outside)
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. Don't use 进去 here — that pushes them away from you.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to say "I learned how to cook"?
options: 我 学 做 菜
我 学会 做 菜 了
我 可以 做 菜
我 想 学 做 菜
exercises.answer: 我 学会 做 菜 了
exercises.explanation: 学会 = study + acquired skill. The result (capability) is the point.

exercises.prompt: Trap: "我 没 看见 你" vs "我 看 不 见 你" — pick the contrast.
options: First: didn't see you (past fact). Second: can't see you (capability now).
exercises.answer: First: didn't see you (past fact). Second: can't see you (capability now).
exercises.explanation: 没 looks back at what happened. 不 inside the complement asks about current capability.

exercises.prompt: Build "She ran out of the house (toward us)"
exercises.answer: 她 跑 出 来 了
exercises.explanation: 跑出来 = run + out + toward speaker. 了 marks completion.

exercises.prompt: "作业 我 还 没 做完, 但 已 经 做 ___ 一半" — fill in (already done half)
exercises.explanation: 已 经 做 了 一半 — neutral past with aspect 了. Don't add 完 if you haven't finished.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: pick the WRONG translation of "I can hear the music"
options: 我 听得见 音乐
我 能 听到 音乐
我 可以 听 音乐
Native uses 听得见 / 听到 — 可以 听 means 'allowed to listen', a different idea
exercises.answer: 我 可以 听 音乐
exercises.explanation: 可以 listen = have permission. Use a potential complement (听得见) or 听到 for actual perception.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 看 不 见 你

我 没 看见 你
我 可以 看见 你

exercises.answer: 我 看 不 见 你
exercises.explanation: 看不见 (kàn bu jiàn) — "can't see you (right now)." Distinct from 没 看见 (didn't see you).

exercises.explanation: 拿下来 = take + down + toward speaker. Combines 把-construction with directional complement — peak B1.

topics.title: Measure word deep dive
topics.description: Beyond 个 — picking the right classifier for the noun: 条, 张, 只, 件, 把, 颗, 杯, 瓶 …

guide.intro: In A1 you learned 个 (the universal MW) and 本 (for books). Mandarin actually has hundreds of measure words — but you only need about a dozen to sound natural. The rule of thumb: shape and category of the noun pick the MW.

sections.text: Shape-based MWs

rows: fish, snakes, roads, pants, dogs (slim ones)

sections.text: Category MWs

rows: most animals; one of a pair

sections.text: Native speakers will understand if you say 一 个 鱼 instead of 一 条 鱼 — but you'll sound like a beginner. Picking the right MW is exactly what makes B1 sound like B1.
The 个 trap
English speakers over-use 个 because it's the safest fallback. Push yourself: when you see a long thin thing, reach for 条; flat → 张; clothing → 件; small round → 颗. Build the reflex.

lessons.title: 条 vs 张 — long vs flat
lessons.description: Shape decides — long-thin uses 条, flat-rectangular uses 张

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 鱼 (one fish)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 票 (three tickets)
exercises.explanation: Tickets are flat sheets → 张. 三 张 票.

exercises.explanation: Roads are long and linear → 条. 一 条 路.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 两 ___ 床 (two beds)
exercises.explanation: Beds are flat / broad surface → 张. 两 张 床.

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW for "a long bench (long thin furniture)": 一 ___ 长椅

topics.title: Opinions & agreement
topics.description: I think, I believe, I agree — saying what you reckon

guide.intro: B1 means saying more than "I like" or "I want". You need ways to express opinions softly, agree, disagree, and ask people what THEY think. Three verbs do the heavy lifting: 觉得, 认为, and 看.

sections.text: 觉得 — feel / think (everyday)
觉得 (jué de) is the workhorse — "I feel / think that...". Use it for any soft, personal opinion. By far the most common in conversation.

rows.source: 我 觉得 这 个 电影 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè ge diànyǐng hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: I think this movie is good.

rows.source: 你 觉得 怎么样？

sections.text: 认为 — believe / hold (more formal)
认为 (rèn wéi) is firmer and more written — "I hold the view that...". Right for opinions on bigger issues, news, business, debate.

rows.source: 我 认为 这 个 计划 不 行。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè ge jìhuà bù xíng.
rows.translation: I don't think this plan will work.

rows.source: 专家 认为 经济 会 好转。
rows.translation: Experts believe the economy will improve.

sections.text: 看 — see / view (informal opinion ask)
看 (kàn) literally means "look", but "你 看 …" idiomatically means "in your view, …". Used to gently ask someone's take.

rows.source: 你 看 我 该 怎么 办？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ kàn wǒ gāi zěnme bàn?
rows.translation: What do you think I should do?

rows.source: 我 看 应该 没 问题。
rows.translation: I think it should be fine.

sections.text: Agreeing & disagreeing
Chinese conversation tends to soften disagreement. "我 不 太 同意" (I don't really agree) is gentler and more common than a flat "不 同意".

topics.title: Telling a story
topics.description: Sequencing past events with 着 and directional verbs

guide.intro: When you narrate a story you need ways to set the scene ("she was sitting"), describe motion ("he walked in"), and string events together. 着 handles ongoing states; directional complements like 上来 and 下去 handle motion in space.

sections.text: 着 — ongoing state
着 (zhe) attached to a verb means "in the state of doing". It's NOT the same as English -ing — 着 emphasizes a held position or background condition, often setting the scene.

rows.source: 他 站 着。
rows.translation: He is standing. (in a standing state)

rows.source: 门 开 着。
她 笑 着 说。

sections.text: 着 vs 在: 在 means "actively doing right now" ("我 在 吃饭" — I'm eating). 着 means "in this state" ("门 开 着" — the door's open). For narration, 着 sets the scene; 在 reports a live action.
Directional complements: 上 / 下 / 进 / 出 / 来 / 去
Six little words combine into rich verbs of motion. Pair a base direction (up/down/in/out) with 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker).

rows.source: 他 走 进来 了。
她 跑 出去 了。
请 上来。

sections.text: Figurative directionals — 起来 / 下去 / 出来
Directional complements stretch beyond physical motion. Attached to non-motion verbs, they signal phase or aspect: starting, continuing, or coming-to-clarity.

rows: 看 起来 很 累 — looks tired

rows.source: 我 终于 想 出来 了。
请 你 说 下 去。
他 突然 笑 起来 了。

sections.text: Sequencing words
A2's 然后 still works, but B1 stories add 先...再... (first...then...), 最后 (finally), 突然 (suddenly), and 后来 (afterward — for events further apart).

rows.source: 我 先 吃饭，再 看 电影。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chīfàn, zài kàn diànyǐng.
rows.translation: First I'll eat, then watch a movie.

rows.source: 突然 下雨 了。
后来 他 搬 走 了。

lessons.title: 了 / 过 / 着 contrast drill
lessons.description: Aspect markers — perfective vs experience vs ongoing state

exercises.prompt: Distinguish: 我 吃 了 饺子 vs 我 吃 过 饺子
options: First: I ate dumplings (specific occasion). Second: I have eaten dumplings (ever, in my life)
First is future, second is past
First is question, second is statement
exercises.answer: First: I ate dumplings (specific occasion). Second: I have eaten dumplings (ever, in my life)
exercises.explanation: 了 = perfective (one occasion completed). 过 = experiential (have you ever).

exercises.prompt: Build "I've been to Beijing twice"
exercises.answer: 我 去 过 两 次 北京

exercises.explanation: 着 = the door is in a state of being open. 了 would emphasize that opening just happened.

exercises.prompt: the aspect to its job
Fill: "我 ___ 看 这 个 电影 ， 不 想 再 看" ("already seen, not again")
Build "It's been raining for three days"
exercises.answer: 已经 下 了 三 天 雨 了
exercises.explanation: 了₁ + duration + 了₂ — "completed three days of rain AND it's still relevant / ongoing". Two 了, two jobs.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right aspect: "He is sitting on the chair"
options: 他 坐 在 椅子 上
他 坐 着 椅子
他 坐 在 椅子 上 着
他 在 坐 椅子 上
exercises.answer: 他 坐 在 椅子 上
exercises.explanation: 坐 在 + place — "sit at". 着 here is implied / not needed since 在 + location locks the state.

exercises.explanation: 吃 过 — experience: "have ever eaten". Listen for the soft 过 vs the harder 了.

exercises.prompt: Build "Have you ever been to Shanghai? — No, I haven't"
exercises.answer: 你 去 过 上海 吗 ？ 没 去 过

exercises.prompt: "我 在 学 中文"
exercises.explanation: 在 + V = active in-progress action. Different from 着 (held state).

exercises.prompt: Build "Yesterday I saw an old movie I'd never seen before"
exercises.answer: 昨天 我 看 了 一 部 没 看 过 的 老 电影
exercises.explanation: 看 了 (perfective — yesterday) + 没 看 过 的 (relative clause — "that I'd never seen"). 了 and 过 in the same sentence.
